sentences.text: This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 29.12.2023 at about 5.00 p.m., the petitioner was on footpath, at BMTC 7th Depo road, Near BMTC 7th Main Gate, Bengaluru City by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

At that time, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-36-F-1253 driven the same at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and the said bus ran over on the both legs of the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, he sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Victoria Hospital,
Mahesha vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116110335/
1
wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery and discharged with an advice to regular follow up treatment.
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
It is specifically urged that due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
It is further urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus.
Respondent being the Insurer cum owner of the bus, is liable to pay the compensation.
3. After service of notice, the respondent appeared before the Court and filed written statement specifically denying the petition averments.
This respondent denied the negligence of the driver of KSRTC bus as the driver and he was not responsible for the alleged accident.
Per contra it is contended that the petitioner was sleeping on the footpath stretching his legs to the service road.
Hence it not the fault of the driver of the bus and it is only due to the fault and negligence of the petitioner.
Rest of the averments of the petition are repudiated as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the pleadings, the tribunal framed following issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 29.12.2023 at about 5.00 p.m, on Footpath,
at BMTC 7th Depo road, near BMTC 7th Main Gate, he sustained grievous injuries due to rash and negligent act of driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-36-F-1253 ?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ? If so, what is the quantum ?
From whom ?
3.
What order or award?
5. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 17 were marked on his behalf.

Dr. B. Ramesh,
Orthopedic Surgeon was examined as PW.2.
Ex's .P18 to 20 were marked through him.

On the other hand Sri. Shanthappa, the driver Cum conductor of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-36-F-1253 was examined as RW.1.
6.
Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondent corporation on merits.
The counsel for petitioner filed written arguments.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

7. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS Mahesha vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116110335/
2 8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ISSUE NO.1 : The petitioner filed evidence affidavit reiterating petition averments.
Ex.P1 is the FIR registered by Upparpet Traffic police against the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-36-F-1253 on the basis of FIS lodged by Police official.
Ex.P8 is the wound certificate issued by Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, which indicates that the petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident.
Spot mahazar Ex.P.3 & Sketch Ex.P.4 corroborate the place of accident.
Ex. P7-IMV report discloses that the brake system of the KSRTC bus was in order and the IMV Inspector has opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said bus.

9. Admittedly the accident occurred at the time when the petitioner herein was sleeping on the footpath but his legs were at road at that time, the driver of KSRTC bus driven the same in a rash and negligent manner ran over on the legs of the petitioner and caused accident.
The respondent corporation and driver of the offending Bus denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.

On perusal of FIR and charge sheet it is clearly mentioned that the bus driver had parked his bus near the main gate of Unit 7, and while leaving, he recklessly drove the bus forward, resulting in the wheels of the bus running over both legs of a person sleeping at the bottom of the same bus,
causing serious injuries.
Thereby it is clear that the driver of the bus without seeing the person who was sleeping on the footpath and moved his bus in recklessly and caused the accident.
But the respondent contended that there is no rash and negligent act of the driver of the bus and the said negligence is on the part of the petitioner himself.

10. In support of his case, the learned counsel for petitioner relied on the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of 1986 AIR 180 between Olga Tellis V/s Bombay Municipal Corporation & others.

entities.text: 1986 AIR 180 between Olga Tellis V/s Bombay Municipal Corporation & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein it is relied on the constitution of India, 1950, Article 32- Fundamental Rights - Estoppel- Principle behind - No Estoppal can be claimed against enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
Further in para No.56 it is clearly observed that :
2.3 In a matter like the one in which the future of half of the city's population is at stake, the Court must consult authentic empirical data compiled by agencies, official and non-official.
It is by that process that the core of the problem can be reached and a satisfactory solution found.

It would be unrealistic on the part of the Court to reject the petitions on the ground that the petitioners have not adduced evidence to show that they will be rendered jobless if they are evicted from the slums and pavements.
Common sense, which is a cluster of life's experiences, is often more dependable than the rival facts presented by warring litigants.

In the instant case, it is clear from the various expert studies that one of the main reasons of the emergence and growth of squatter-settlements in big Metropolitan cities like Bombay, is the availability of job opportunities which are lacking in the rural sector.
The undisputed fact that even after eviction, the squatters return to the cities affords proof of that position.

These facts constitute empirical evidence to justify the conclusion that persons in the position of petitioners live in slums and on pavements because they have small jobs to nurse in the city and there is nowhere else to live.
Evidently, they choose a pavement or a slum in the vicinity of their place of work, the time otherwise taken in commuting and its cost being forbidding for their slender means.
To lose the pavement or the slum is to lose the job.

The conclusion, therefore, in terms of the Mahesha vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116110335/
3

entities.text: Mahesha vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: constitutional phraseology is that the eviction of the petitioners will lead to deprivation of their livelihood and consequently to the deprivation of life.
In the above matter it is mentioned as squatter-settlements in big Metropolitan cities like Bombay, is the availability of job opportunities which are lacking in the rural sector.
The undisputed fact that even after eviction, the squatters return to the cities affords proof of that position.

These facts constitute empirical evidence to justify the conclusion that persons in the position of petitioners live in slums and on pavements because they have small jobs to nurse in the city and there is nowhere else to live.
Evidently, they choose a pavement or a slum in the vicinity of their place of work, the time otherwise taken in commuting and its cost being forbidding for their slender means.
To lose the pavement or the slum is to lose the job.

The conclusion,
therefore, in terms of the constitutional phraseology is that the eviction of the petitioners will lead to deprivation of their livelihood and consequently to the deprivation of life.
In the present case also as per the contentions of the petitioner, petitioner came to Bengaluru for searching the job.
When he was sleeping at footpath, the said incident happened.
In the above decision it is clear that the KSRTC bus driver did not have sufficient cause to cause the accident.
The fact that accident is occurred at 7.45 p.m, yet he did not see the person who was sleeping on the footpath, leads to drawing of an inference that he was moved his bus negligently.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet (Ex.P10) against him for the offences punishable under section's 279 & 338 of IPC and u/s 134(a&b), 187 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
12. In the instant case there is no dispute with respect to the police documents produced by the petitioner which were prepared by the police while discharging official duty.
Said documents manifest that the accident in question had taken place purely due to the negligence on part of the KSRTC bus driver.

It is noteworthy to state that the self serving statement of the driver of the offending bus (RW.1) cannot be attached any evidentiary value as he would obviously give a different version of the accident to escape from the criminal liability which would in turn affect his employment prospects.

13. Moreover it is settled law that the term 'rashness and negligence' has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the M.V Act as compared to the word 'rashness and negligence' as finds mention in the IPC.
This is because the chapter in M.V Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, based on the above discussion I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC is proved.

Accordingly this issue is answered in the 'Affirmative'.
14.
ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of KSRTC Bus.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.

Mahesha vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116110335/
4
15. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :

The petitioner has exhibited his Aadhar card at Ex.P17,
wherein his date of birth is reflected as 01.01.1994.
This indicates that he was aged (29 years 11 months 28 days) 30 years on the date of accident.
16. The petitioner deposed that prior to the accident he was working as Labourer and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
No documents have been produced to establish the avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in his evidence affidavit.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.

17. As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : (1) Left leg closed mid shaft femur fracture, (2) Left leg closed mid shaft of both bones fracture (3) 5th Metatarsal fracture of left foot and (4) Degloving injury of left foot.
It is needless to say that the injury is grievous in nature.
The discharge summary of Victoria Hospital (Ex.P.12) indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 29.12.2023 to 07.01.2024 (10 days in total).
During the course of treatment he had undergone surgeries in the form of : internal fixation of left femur, tibia fibula K-wire fixation heel pad avulsion.
18. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.B. Ramesh as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total permanent physical disability of 50% to the left lower limb and 25% disability to the whole body.
It is elicited during the course of cross examination PW.2 categorically admitted that he was not treated the petitioner.
Further he admitted that at the time of discharge the petitioner was stable and these types of injuries required 6 months to recover.
He further admitted that the petitioner can do his day-to-day activities with lot of difficulty.
Femur fracture is united, tibia fracture is non united.
Metatarsal fracture is united and implants are in situ.
When such is the case physical disability assessed by the medical expert is on the higher side.
Be that as it may, the law is Mahesha vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 September, 2025
Indian

Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116110335/
5 well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctors, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 15%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 15%.
19. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES : The period of hospitalization of 10 days is proved with a help of discharge summary.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day and a sum of Rs.12,000/- (1,200 X 10) is awarded under this head.
20. PAIN & SUFFERINGS : On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.

21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital
, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 4 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards Rs.64,000/- (16,000 X 4) under this head.
22. MEDICAL EXPENSES :

As per the bills marked at Ex.P14, the petitioner has spent Rs.5,042/-
towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of his cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,042/- which is rounded off to Rs.5,000/- towards medical expenses.
23. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '17'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.4,89,600/- (Rs.16,000 X 12 X 17 X 15%) is awarded under this head.
24. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded under this head.
25. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for non union of left tibia, infection of heel pad, and implants removal.

No Mahesha vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116110335/
6 estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.

entities.text: No Mahesha vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgery for removal of implants, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.20,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

26. The calculation table stands as follows :
1
Attendant charges, extra : 12,000-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 2 Pain & sufferings : 50,000-00 3 Loss of income during laid-up : 64,000-00 period
4 Medical expenses : 5,000-00 5 Loss of future income due to : 4,89,600-00 disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 50,000-00 happiness 7

Future medical expenses :
20,000-00 Total 6,90,600-00 27.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Considering the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
The Respondent being the RC owner/insurer of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA- 36-F-1253 is liable and directed to pay the compensation amount.

With this observation,
issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the affirmative'.
28.
ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.6,90,600/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (Excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and printout taken by him, then corrected and pronounced by me in the open court on this the 6th day of September - 2025)
(Shreyansh Doddamani) XXI Addl.
Small Causes Judge & ACJM, Bengaluru.
